metric: Knight (classic) smothered mates per 100 games, 5s + 0.05s per move
baseline_note: B = development settings: SmotherClassic true, SmotherBuildKnightCheck 16, SmotherCrushQuiet 3, SmotherCrushMoves 16.

experiments.title: Prep phase: keep the smother ingredients before construction
experiments.question: Does a bonus for keeping our knight and queen and the enemy's pieces and king-side pawns between +4 and +8 raise knight smothers?
experiments.verdict: No gain against Stockfish 1500; differences elsewhere within noise. Stays off.

experiments.title: Small neural network as the construction score
experiments.question: A 16-neuron network predicts knight smothers better than the hand score (AUC 0.968 vs 0.936). Does it give more smothers in games?
experiments.verdict: At x6 it ties the hand score; stronger settings give up material chasing the network and lose games. Off by default.

experiments.title: Learned linear model as the construction score
experiments.question: 17 hand features fitted to 4.5M positions (AUC 0.936) instead of the hand-written terms.
experiments.verdict: Peaks near x20, equal to the hand score. Off by default.

experiments.title: Aiming for knight smothers
experiments.question: 1.5 aims at any smother. What do SmotherClassic and the knight-route bonus (KnightCheck) give?
experiments.verdict: About 5-6 times more knight smothers; the basis of the 1.6 settings.

strength.title: Prover time in undecided positions off vs on
strength.verdict: The prover costs no measurable strength.

audits: 83% of knight smothers close the box with the defender's forced reply to a check in the final sequence (2,481 smothers).
In stalled won positions, a forced knight smother existed in 2 of 120 positions with one open square, even with a much larger prover budget.
One-move traps against the real opponent (Stockfish 1500) were available in 1 of 240 stalled positions.
The engine's expected defender reply matched the real reply 81% of the time in construction mode.
